meta.title: Francis Quin — Product Engineer
meta.description: Product Engineer focused on frontend. I build complete web products: from complex systems to clear interfaces.

hero.title: I turn complex systems into clear products.
hero.subtitle: I've spent years building web products end to end: first full stack with Ruby on Rails, now frontend with React and TypeScript at Webel. I work across architecture, interface and product, and increasingly close to AI applied to building software.
hero.scrollHint: Scroll to bring the system into order
hero.sceneLabel: Abstract visualization: a scattered cloud of nodes that reorganizes into a structured form as you scroll

webel.title: Webel
webel.intro: A services marketplace with thousands of users and an active product team. I work as a Frontend Developer across the whole platform.

areas.name: Webel Business
areas.description: The B2B side of the platform: service procurement for companies, with its own flows, permissions and purchasing cycle.

areas.name: Internal dashboard
areas.description: Operations tooling for the team: user, service and incident management, plus business metrics.

areas.name: Programmatic SEO
areas.description: Large-scale page generation to capture search demand: templates, structured data and carefully tuned performance.

areas.name: Core marketplace
areas.description: The main product: search, booking and tracking of services between customers and professionals.

projects.title: Things I've built
projects.intro: Products in production, my own systems and experiments. Ordered by where my energy goes now.

items.title: Understand before building
items.description: Code is the cheap part. Before writing a line, I ask who it's for, what problem it solves and how we'll know it works.

items.title: Reduce complexity
items.description: A complex system is no excuse for a complex interface. My job is to absorb that complexity and hand back something people grasp at first sight.

items.title: Design for change
items.description: Today's product won't be next year's. I build systems out of pieces you can swap without tearing the whole building down.

items.title: AI as an amplifier
items.description: I use agents and models to explore faster, automate the repetitive and reach the decisions that matter sooner. The tool amplifies; the judgment stays mine.

skills.title: From server to pixel, and from pixel to business

experience.title: Full stack → frontend → product
experience.evolutionNote: The direction is clear: each stage has brought me closer to where engineering meets product. The next one is AI-powered product engineering.

contact.title: Shall we build something?
contact.intro: I'm drawn to teams building real products and to projects where engineering and product overlap. If that sounds like what you're working on, write to me.
